title: Col. Robert Patterson builds Lexington
summary: In April 1779 Robert Patterson led about twenty-five men from Harrodsburg and began the fort at Lexington, then helped lay off the town.
bodyMarkdown:
In April 1779 Ensign Robert Patterson led about twenty-five men north from Harrodsburg and began a fort on the site that became Lexington, naming the place for the Massachusetts battle that opened the Revolution. He helped lay off the town, sat for years on its board of trustees, and later helped charter Transylvania University.

In 1788 he partnered with Matthias Denman and John Filson to found Losantiville (renamed Cincinnati in 1790); he also had a hand in Dayton. His 1780 cabin—moved more than once—stands again on Transylvania’s campus near Third and Broadway.
Source: [https://history.ky.gov/markers/patterson-cabin](https://history.ky.gov/markers/patterson-cabin)
